capabilities: Draw and edit chemical structures and reactions with the Ketcher editor
Render and edit SMILES, MOL, CDXML, and RXN files via standard embeds and code blocks
Calculate stoichiometry, yields, and green metrics in ELN code blocks
Manage compound libraries, inventories, and LIMS dashboards with chem-db blocks
View and edit biological sequences (DNA, RNA, peptides) in FASTA, HELM, and related formats
extras: The ELN is described as experimental, and .cdxml support relies on Ketcher's open-source conversion engine, so complex ChemDraw-specific objects may not render correctly. Auto-naming and PubChem searches require an internet connection; the plugin also offers a fully offline mode.
intentEvidence: ChemEdit combines features that would otherwise require several plugins
motivation: The author wanted a dedicated electronic lab notebook experience in Obsidian with seamless, visual molecule editing and native support for SMILES, CDXML, and MOL files.
problem: Obsidian has no native way to draw, edit, or render chemical structures and reactions inside notes.

relations.evidence: Their fantastic work provided the initial inspiration to build this tool
Integration with Obsidian Canvas and Excalidraw

summary: Chemical structure editor and viewer powered by Ketcher and SmilesDrawer that renders and edits SMILES, MOL, and CDXML files and adds an electronic lab notebook.
